```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(gflow)
if (!exists("knn_build_identity")) knn_build_identity <- get.gflow.build.identity()
artifact_dir <- if (exists("knn_artifact_dir")) knn_artifact_dir else
    file.path(tempdir(), "gflow-knn-vignette")
dir.create(artifact_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
dir.create(file.path(artifact_dir, "figures"), showWarnings = FALSE)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
    collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", warning = TRUE, message = FALSE,
    fig.width = 8.4, fig.height = 4.8, dpi = 144, fig.retina = 2,
    dev = "png", out.width = "100%",
    cache.path = paste0(file.path(artifact_dir, "cache"), "/"),
    cache.extra = list(build = knn_build_identity$build.id,
                       runtime = knn_build_identity$runtime$id,
                       R = R.version.string)
)
# pkgdown must keep figures under the vignette's relative output directory
# so its article builder can copy them into the published site.
if (!identical(Sys.getenv("IN_PKGDOWN"), "true")) {
    knitr::opts_chunk$set(fig.path = paste0(file.path(artifact_dir, "figures"), "/"))
}
knitr::opts_knit$set(progress = TRUE)
```

`knn.basins()` identifies extrema of an outcome `y` at the rows of a data
matrix `X`. It uses all supplied coordinates, with no PCA, scaling, or outcome
smoothing. This vignette follows three examples: a known one-dimensional
function, an irregularly sampled two-dimensional surface, and the Maunga Whau
terrain data supplied with R.

The examples separate three decisions. **Neighborhood size** sets the spatial
scale at which a point must dominate its neighbors. **Persistence** measures
vertical separation from an older extremum. **Minimum basin size** requires
enough assigned observations after persistence merging. A narrow, distinct
feature can pass the persistence threshold and still fail the size threshold.

## What the function returns

By default (`symmetrize = TRUE`), each observation selects its `k` nearest
other observations. A connection is
included if either endpoint selects the other, giving an undirected,
union-symmetrized kNN neighborhood. L2 uses Euclidean distance; Linfty uses
the largest absolute coordinate difference. Connected observations with exactly
equal outcomes form one plateau. A plateau chooses its nearest improving
boundary edge, and following those choices produces the initial flow basins.

For maxima, persistence is the peak height minus the level where its
superlevel component joins a component with an older peak. Minima reverse
the construction: persistence is the merge level minus the trough height.
Higher maxima and lower minima are older; equal-height extrema use the
smaller representative row. Each connected component has one essential
extremum per direction, with infinite persistence and no finite merge level.

| Stage | Returned labels | Rule |
|---|---|---|
| Initial flow | `initial.labels` | Follow nearest improving plateaus. |
| Persistence merging | `persistence.labels` | Merge extrema with persistence strictly below the threshold into surviving ancestors. |
| Size filtering | `labels` | Set labels to `NA` in remaining basins with fewer than the required observations. |

Labels are representative **row indices**, not sequential cluster numbers.
The `max` and `min` results are separate partitions; their labels and colors
do not identify the same regions. Size filtering does not reassign excluded
observations. Merged labels are unions of initial basins, and these unions
can be disconnected when an intervening basin remains retained. They should
not be interpreted as physical drainage catchments.

## Choosing the neighborhood rule

Use `symmetrize = FALSE` to test each row against **exactly its own `k`
nearest other rows**. Incoming selections do not enlarge the test. A maximum
has no strictly higher selected neighbor; a minimum has no strictly lower
selected neighbor. The query point itself is implicit in this comparison.

```{r directed-neighborhood-example}
toy_X <- matrix(c(0, 1, 3.5))
toy_y <- c(0, 5, 10)
toy_union <- knn.basins(toy_X, toy_y, k = 1)
toy_directed <- knn.basins(toy_X, toy_y, k = 1, symmetrize = FALSE)
knitr::kable(data.frame(
    row = 1:3, position = toy_X[, 1], outcome = toy_y,
    selected.neighbor = toy_directed$neighborhood$knn.index[, 1],
    union.maximum = 1:3 %in% toy_union$max$extrema$row,
    directed.maximum = 1:3 %in% toy_directed$max$extrema$row
), row.names = FALSE)
stopifnot(identical(toy_union$max$extrema$row, 3L),
          identical(toy_directed$max$extrema$row, c(3L, 2L)),
          identical(toy_directed$max$initial.labels, c(2L, 2L, 3L)))
```

Row 2 selects row 1, whose outcome is lower, so row 2 passes the directed
maximum test. Row 3 selects row 2. Symmetrization adds that incoming connection
to row 2's neighborhood, disqualifying it as a maximum in the default mode.

Directed basin assignment uses the same `CLOSEST` principle as gflow's
graph-based trajectory flow: take the **shortest outgoing edge that strictly
improves the outcome**, then repeat. Distance ties use the smaller target row.
The endpoint identifies the initial basin. A much larger outcome gain cannot
override a nearer improving neighbor. This is a local step rule, not a
minimum-total-length path optimization. It does not impose an absolute
edge-length cutoff: if the only improving selected neighbor is far away,
the step still uses that neighbor. Each direction's `next.vertex` records
these successors, with `NA` at terminal extrema.

Equal-valued rows are not contracted in directed mode. A row with no strictly
improving selected neighbor stops even if an equal neighbor can move farther
uphill or downhill. This preserves the exact per-row test, but flat regions
can contain many terminal extrema.

The directed mode therefore also changes the meaning of `persistence` to
**directed escape prominence**. Starting at a maximum, consider paths that
follow outgoing kNN connections to a strictly higher terminal maximum. The
escape level is the highest possible minimum outcome along such a path.
Prominence is the starting height minus that level. Minima reverse the
inequalities. These escape paths can descend, ascend, or cross equal values;
they are different from the strictly improving basin trajectories.

There is no finite escape level when no strictly more extreme terminal row
is reachable. Both maxima in the small example have infinite directed
prominence: row 2 cannot reach row 3 through its outgoing connections, even
though the underlying undirected graph is connected. Equal-height terminal
extrema do not eliminate one another. Several essential extrema can thus
exist in one weak component, and infinity does not establish statistical
importance. This convention is not ordinary connected-component persistence.

The filtering sequence remains the same: extrema with prominence strictly
below `min.persistence` merge along their parent links; then basins smaller
than `min.basin.size` receive `NA` labels. Initial trajectories are preserved,
and merging does not create a new shortest-edge ascent/descent path.

The synthetic figures and the first terrain figures below use the default
symmetric mode. A separate terrain comparison holds the numeric settings
fixed and displays both modes side by side; the neighborhood-scale sensitivity
analysis then returns to symmetric mode.

```{r plotting-helpers, include=FALSE}
ink <- "#253943"
muted <- "#667780"
excluded <- "#cbd1d3"
# Extra distinguishable shades are needed for the initial, unmerged basins.
# Representative-row labels supply a redundant identity cue.
basin_palette <- c("#216b9b", "#b78016", "#a64c73", "#548342", "#7860a7",
                   "#bd683b", "#398f89", "#606c7a", "#b75043", "#8a793e")
theme_par <- function(...) par(fg = ink, col.axis = ink, col.lab = ink,
                               col.main = ink, family = "sans", las = 1, cex = 1, ...)
fmt <- function(x, digits = 3) ifelse(is.infinite(x), "essential",
                                     formatC(x, format = "f", digits = digits))
summary_stages <- function(fit, example) {
    do.call(rbind, lapply(c("max", "min"), function(direction) {
        z <- fit[[direction]]
        do.call(rbind, lapply(c("initial.labels", "persistence.labels", "labels"), function(stage) {
            labels <- z[[stage]]
            data.frame(example = example, direction = direction,
                       stage = c(initial.labels = "Initial", persistence.labels = "Persistence",
                                 labels = "Size filter")[[stage]],
                       basins = length(unique(labels[!is.na(labels)])),
                       unassigned = sum(is.na(labels)), n = length(labels))
        }))
    }))
}
colors_for <- function(labels, fit, direction, X = NULL, reference = fit) {
    rows <- reference[[direction]]$extrema$row
    key <- setNames(rep(basin_palette, length.out = length(rows)), rows)
    if (!identical(fit, reference)) {
        other <- fit[[direction]]$extrema$row
        nearest <- vapply(other, function(i)
            which.min(rowSums(sweep(X[rows, , drop = FALSE], 2, X[i, ], "-")^2)), integer(1))
        key <- setNames(unname(key[nearest]), other)
    }
    color <- unname(key[as.character(labels)])
    color[is.na(labels)] <- excluded
    color
}
plot_ribbons <- function(fit, x, direction) {
    theme_par(mar = c(2.6, 6.2, 1.8, .8), mgp = c(1.6, .45, 0))
    plot(range(x) + c(-.15, .15), c(.5, 3.5), type = "n", yaxt = "n",
         xlab = if (direction == "min") "Location x" else "",
         ylab = "", main = if (direction == "max") "Basins toward maxima" else "Basins toward minima",
         cex.main = .94, xaxs = "i")
    axis(2, at = 3:1, labels = c("Initial", "Persistence", "Size filter"), tick = FALSE, cex.axis = .84)
    dx <- diff(x)[1] / 2
    for (i in 1:3) {
        labels <- fit[[direction]][[c("initial.labels", "persistence.labels", "labels")[i]]]
        rect(x - dx, 4 - i - .29, x + dx, 4 - i + .29,
             col = colors_for(labels, fit, direction), border = NA)
        for (label in unique(labels[!is.na(labels)])) {
            at <- median(x[labels == label & !is.na(labels)])
            text(at, 4 - i, label, col = "white", cex = .70, font = 2)
        }
    }
    box(col = "#cbd1d3")
}
basin_map <- function(X, fit, direction, stage, title, contour_data = NULL,
                      reference = fit, raster_dim = NULL, annotate = TRUE,
                      color_key = NULL, subtitle = NULL, padding = 0) {
    theme_par(mar = c(3.2, 3.2, if (is.null(subtitle)) 2.1 else 3.1, .7),
              mgp = c(1.9, .6, 0), cex.axis = .8, cex.lab = .86)
    labels <- fit[[direction]][[stage]]
    cols <- if (is.null(color_key)) colors_for(labels, fit, direction, X, reference) else {
        color <- unname(color_key[as.character(labels)])
        color[is.na(labels)] <- excluded
        stopifnot(!anyNA(color))
        color
    }
    xlim <- range(X[, 1]); ylim <- range(X[, 2])
    xlim <- xlim + c(-1, 1) * padding * diff(xlim)
    ylim <- ylim + c(-1, 1) * padding * diff(ylim)
    plot(X, type = "n", asp = 1, xlab = if (is.null(raster_dim)) "Coordinate 1" else "Row-axis offset (m)",
         ylab = if (is.null(raster_dim)) "Coordinate 2" else "Column-axis offset (m)",
         main = title, cex.main = .93, xaxs = "i", yaxs = "i", xlim = xlim, ylim = ylim)
    if (!is.null(subtitle)) mtext(subtitle, side = 3, line = .2, cex = .78, col = muted)
    if (is.null(raster_dim)) {
        points(X, pch = 16, col = cols, cex = .42)
    } else {
        palette <- unique(cols)
        image(sort(unique(X[, 1])), sort(unique(X[, 2])),
              matrix(match(cols, palette), nrow = raster_dim[1]),
              col = palette, breaks = seq(.5, length(palette) + .5), add = TRUE, useRaster = TRUE)
    }
    if (!is.null(contour_data)) contour(contour_data$x, contour_data$y, contour_data$z,
                                       levels = contour_data$levels, add = TRUE,
                                       drawlabels = FALSE, col = "#263b4355", lwd = .65)
    active <- unique(labels[!is.na(labels)])
    points(X[active, , drop = FALSE], pch = if (direction == "max") 24 else 25,
           bg = "white", col = ink, cex = .85, lwd = 1)
    if (annotate) {
        # Label only extrema away from the panel edge, where labels are legible.
        span <- apply(X, 2, range)
        interior <- apply(X[active, , drop = FALSE], 1, function(z)
            all(z > span[1, ] + .07 * diff(span) & z < span[2, ] - .07 * diff(span)))
        a <- active[interior]
        text(X[a, , drop = FALSE], labels = a, pos = 3, cex = .65, col = ink)
    }
    box()
}
boundary_extrema <- function(fit, X, direction) {
    ranges <- apply(X, 2, range)
    vapply(fit[[direction]]$extrema$plateau.rows, function(rows)
        any(vapply(seq_len(ncol(X)), function(j)
            any(X[rows, j] %in% ranges[, j]), logical(1))), logical(1))
}
```

## 1. A one-dimensional function with broad and narrow features

We sample 1,000 equally spaced locations on \([0,10]\). The outcome is the
sum of six Gaussian terms,

\[
f(x)=\sum_j a_j\exp\left\{-\frac{(x-\mu_j)^2}{2s_j^2}\right\}.
\]

Positive and negative amplitudes produce peaks and troughs. The components
overlap, so their centers need not be extrema of the combined function.
Coordinates and outcome heights have arbitrary, fixed units.

```{r one-data, cache=TRUE}
components <- data.frame(
    amplitude = c(2, .5, -1.1, 1.25, -.85, 1.6),
    center = c(2.3, 3.35, 4.55, 5, 5.45, 7.3),
    width = c(.72, .10, .38, .055, .24, 1)
)
f1 <- function(x) rowSums(matrix(vapply(seq_len(nrow(components)), function(j) {
    with(components[j, ], amplitude * exp(-.5 * ((x - center) / width)^2))
}, numeric(length(x))), nrow = length(x)))
X1 <- matrix(seq(0, 10, length.out = 1000), ncol = 1)
y1 <- f1(X1[, 1])
one <- knn.basins(X1, y1, k = 25, metric = "L2",
                  min.persistence = .25, min.basin.size = 100)
```

```{r one-components, echo=FALSE}
knitr::kable(components, digits = 3, caption = "Components of the specified 1D function.")
```

These illustrative thresholds require 0.25 outcome units of persistence and
100 assigned observations. They are chosen to expose the different decisions,
not estimated as optimal settings. The noisy comparison below uses the same
thresholds. All three stages in the figure come from this single function call.

```{r one-stages, echo=FALSE, fig.height=7.2, fig.cap="The exact 1D field and the three assignment stages. Upward triangles mark original maxima; downward triangles mark original minima. Labels in the strips are representative rows, with consistent colors within each direction. Gray denotes observations excluded by the size filter. Dashed segments show two finite maximum merge levels on the kNN graph; these need not equal continuous-curve saddle levels because kNN edges can jump across narrow features.", fig.alt="A curve with broad peaks, a shallow shoulder and a narrow peak above six colored strips showing persistence merging and size filtering."}
local({
    op <- par(no.readonly = TRUE); on.exit(par(op))
    layout(matrix(1:3, ncol = 1), heights = c(2.4, 1.25, 1.25))
    theme_par(mar = c(2.6, 6.2, 1.6, .8), mgp = c(2.6, .7, 0))
    plot(X1[, 1], y1, type = "l", lwd = 1.6, col = ink, xlab = "",
         ylab = "Outcome (arbitrary units)", ylim = c(-1.2, 2.35),
         xlim = range(X1) + c(-.15, .15), xaxs = "i")
    for (direction in c("max", "min")) {
        tab <- one[[direction]]$extrema
        points(X1[tab$row, 1], tab$value, pch = if (direction == "max") 24 else 25,
               bg = "white", col = ink, cex = 1)
    }
    selected <- one$max$extrema[one$max$extrema$status != "retained", ]
    for (i in seq_len(nrow(selected))) {
        xx <- X1[selected$row[i], 1]
        segments(xx - .20, selected$merge.level[i], xx + .20, selected$merge.level[i],
                 col = "#a64c73", lty = 2, lwd = 1.2)
    }
    text(c(3.32, 5.0), c(1.52, 1.02), c("Shallow shoulder", "Narrow peak"), cex = .82)
    plot_ribbons(one, X1[, 1], "max")
    plot_ribbons(one, X1[, 1], "min")
})
```

```{r one-table, echo=FALSE}
one_max_table <- transform(one$max$extrema, location = X1[row, 1])
knitr::kable(one_max_table[, c("row", "location", "value", "merge.level", "persistence",
                              "local.gap", "initial.size", "merged.size", "status")],
              digits = c(0, 3, 3, 3, 3, 5, 0, 0, 0),
              caption = "All original maxima. Merged size is measured before the size filter; a merged extremum has size zero. Inf denotes an essential extremum.")
shoulder1 <- one$max$extrema[one$max$extrema$status == "merged", ]
narrow1 <- one$max$extrema[one$max$extrema$status == "filtered_size", ]
```

The shoulder has persistence `r fmt(shoulder1$persistence)`, below 0.25, and
merges into an older maximum. The narrow peak has persistence
`r fmt(narrow1$persistence)` but only `r narrow1$merged.size` assigned
observations, so the size filter excludes it. This peak is part of the
generating function: **small support does not establish that a feature is
spurious**. Both broad peaks have small local gaps despite substantial
persistence. The gap compares a peak with its best neighboring value, which
can be nearly equal near a smooth summit.

The endpoints are also local minima relative to the sampled domain. Their
basins describe the finite interval, not evidence of additional interior
troughs. Increasing `k` can change both extrema and merge levels by adding
connections across intervening features.

### Add noise without changing the underlying function

```{r one-noise, cache=TRUE, dependson="one-data"}
set.seed(22061)
y_noisy <- y1 + rnorm(length(y1), sd = .03)
noisy <- knn.basins(X1, y_noisy, k = 25,
                    min.persistence = .25, min.basin.size = 100)
```

```{r noise-and-support, echo=FALSE, fig.height=4.1, fig.cap="Left: the exact function and one Gaussian-noise realization, with standard deviation 0.03 outcome units. Markers identify retained noisy-data extrema. Right: original, exact-field maxima plotted by initial assigned size and persistence; shapes show their final decisions. The horizontal dashed line is the persistence threshold. The essential maximum occupies a separately labeled band, not a finite persistence value. Size filtering uses sizes after merging, as reported in the table.", fig.alt="A noisy 1D curve alongside a scatterplot separating a shallow shoulder from a narrow, persistent peak."}
local({
    op <- par(no.readonly = TRUE); on.exit(par(op)); par(mfrow = c(1, 2))
    theme_par(mar = c(4, 4, 2, .8), mgp = c(2.5, .7, 0), cex.axis = .85)
    plot(X1[, 1], y_noisy, pch = 16, cex = .25, col = "#a2abb0",
         xlab = "Location x", ylab = "Outcome", main = "Exact function plus noise", cex.main = 1)
    lines(X1[, 1], y1, col = ink, lwd = 1.5)
    for (d in c("max", "min")) {
        tab <- noisy[[d]]$extrema; tab <- tab[tab$retained, ]
        points(X1[tab$row, 1], tab$value, pch = if (d == "max") 24 else 25,
               bg = "white", col = "#216b9b", cex = 1)
    }
    legend("topright", c("Exact", "Observed"), col = c(ink, "#a2abb0"),
           lty = c(1, NA), pch = c(NA, 16), bty = "n", cex = .78)
    tab <- one$max$extrema
    cap <- max(tab$persistence[is.finite(tab$persistence)]) * 1.23
    plotted <- ifelse(tab$essential, cap, tab$persistence)
    plot(tab$initial.size, plotted, type = "n", xlim = c(0, 520), ylim = c(0, cap * 1.08),
         xlab = "Initial assigned observations", ylab = "Persistence (outcome units)",
         main = "Height and support differ", cex.main = 1, yaxt = "n")
    axis(2, at = c(0, 1, 2), labels = c("0", "1", "2"), cex.axis = .78)
    text(10, cap, "Essential", adj = c(0, .5), cex = .78)
    abline(h = cap * .92, col = "#cbd1d3", lty = 3)
    abline(h = .25, col = muted, lty = 2)
    pch <- c(retained = 21, merged = 24, filtered_size = 22)[tab$status]
    points(tab$initial.size, plotted, pch = pch, bg = colors_for(tab$row, one, "max"),
           col = ink, cex = 1.3)
    text(tab$initial.size, plotted, tab$row,
         pos = ifelse(tab$status == "merged", 4, 3), cex = .8)
    legend("right", c("Retained", "Merged", "Size-filtered"), pch = c(21, 24, 22),
           pt.bg = "white", bty = "n", cex = .75)
})
```

With noise, the initial counts change from `r nrow(one$max$extrema)` to
`r nrow(noisy$max$extrema)` maxima and from `r nrow(one$min$extrema)` to
`r nrow(noisy$min$extrema)` minima. The final counts are
`r sum(noisy$max$extrema$retained)` maxima and
`r sum(noisy$min$extrema$retained)` minima. Agreement in counts is not proof
of exact recovery: the representative locations and memberships also change.
No smoothing has been applied. If a smoothed outcome is supplied, its
estimation settings become an additional part of the analysis.

## 2. An irregularly sampled two-dimensional surface

The next surface contains two broad elevated regions, a shoulder near the
left region, two depressions, and a narrow positive feature. Coordinates are
in the same arbitrary distance units. The tilted first Gaussian makes the
geometry anisotropic. We evaluate the surface at 2,000 uniformly sampled
locations in \([-3,3]^2\), without observational noise.

```{r two-data, cache=TRUE}
f2 <- function(X) {
    bump <- function(cx, cy, sx, sy, theta = 0) {
        u <- cos(theta) * (X[, 1] - cx) + sin(theta) * (X[, 2] - cy)
        v <- -sin(theta) * (X[, 1] - cx) + cos(theta) * (X[, 2] - cy)
        exp(-.5 * ((u / sx)^2 + (v / sy)^2))
    }
    2.4 * bump(-1.35, .7, .8, .55, pi / 9) +
        .9 * bump(-.3, 1, .22, .22) +
        1.8 * bump(1.3, .7, .7, .8) -
        1.6 * bump(-.7, -1.4, .6, .6) -
        .8 * bump(1.6, -1.6, .5, .4) +
        1.5 * bump(0, -.6, .1, .1)
}
set.seed(22062)
X2 <- matrix(runif(4000, -3, 3), ncol = 2)
y2 <- f2(X2)
two <- knn.basins(X2, y2, k = 25, metric = "L2",
                  min.persistence = .3, min.basin.size = 100)
two_linf <- knn.basins(X2, y2, k = 25, metric = "Linfty",
                       min.persistence = .3, min.basin.size = 100)
```

```{r two-surface, echo=FALSE, fig.height=5.1, fig.cap="The specified continuous surface, evaluated on a dense display grid, with the 2,000 actual input locations overlaid as small dots. Contours and the color key use outcome units. Only the irregular observations enter knn.basins(); the display grid is not analyzed. The narrow feature near (0, -0.6) is part of the known surface.", fig.alt="A contour and color map of the two broad peaks, two depressions and narrow peak, with irregularly sampled input locations."}
display_axis <- seq(-3, 3, length.out = 151)
display_X <- as.matrix(expand.grid(display_axis, display_axis))
display_z <- matrix(f2(display_X), length(display_axis))
contours2 <- list(x = display_axis, y = display_axis, z = display_z,
                  levels = c(-1.2, -.6, 0, .6, 1.2, 1.8, 2.4))
local({
    op <- par(no.readonly = TRUE); on.exit(par(op))
    theme_par(mar = c(4, 4, 1.2, 1))
    filled.contour(display_axis, display_axis, display_z,
                   color.palette = function(n) hcl.colors(n, "Blue-Red 3", rev = TRUE),
                   asp = 1, xlab = "Coordinate 1", ylab = "Coordinate 2",
                   key.title = title(main = "Outcome", cex.main = .85),
                   plot.axes = {
                       axis(1); axis(2)
                       contour(display_axis, display_axis, display_z, levels = contours2$levels,
                               add = TRUE, col = "#263b4377", labcex = .65)
                       points(X2, pch = 16, cex = .12, col = "#25394355")
                   })
})
```

```{r two-basins, echo=FALSE, fig.width=9, fig.height=6.7, fig.cap="Rows distinguish maximum-oriented and minimum-oriented basins. Columns compare initial L2 assignments, final L2 assignments, and final Linfty assignments at the same k and filtering thresholds. Contours are held fixed. Colors for Linfty extrema are matched to the nearest original L2 extremum of the same direction; numerical labels remain the actual representative rows. Gray points are size-filtered. Boundary candidates in the initial maps are features of the finite sampled neighborhood.", fig.alt="Six basin maps comparing original L2 basins with filtered L2 and Linfty basins for maxima and minima."}
local({
    op <- par(no.readonly = TRUE); on.exit(par(op)); par(mfrow = c(2, 3))
    for (d in c("max", "min")) {
        label <- if (d == "max") "Maxima" else "Minima"
        basin_map(X2, two, d, "initial.labels", paste(label, "- initial L2"), contours2)
        basin_map(X2, two, d, "labels", paste(label, "- final L2"), contours2)
        basin_map(X2, two_linf, d, "labels", paste(label, "- final Linfty"), contours2, reference = two)
    }
})
```

```{r two-table, echo=FALSE}
interior2 <- two$max$extrema[abs(X2[two$max$extrema$row, 1]) < 2.7 &
                              abs(X2[two$max$extrema$row, 2]) < 2.7, ]
knitr::kable(interior2[, c("row", "value", "persistence", "initial.size", "merged.size", "status")],
              digits = 3, caption = "Interior maximum candidates under L2; boundary candidates remain in the complete result.")
narrow2 <- two$max$extrema[which.min(rowSums(sweep(X2[two$max$extrema$row, ], 2, c(0, -.6), "-")^2)), ]
```

The narrow peak has `r narrow2$initial.size` initial observations and
persistence `r fmt(narrow2$persistence)`. It survives the 0.3 persistence
threshold but fails the 100-observation requirement. This is another known
surface feature removed by a deliberate support requirement. The final L2
result retains `r sum(two$max$extrema$retained)` maxima and
`r sum(two$min$extrema$retained)` minima.

L2 distance balls are circular; Linfty distance balls are axis-aligned squares.
They can connect different pairs of observations and produce different
assignments even when the retained counts agree. Linfty also depends on the
chosen coordinate axes. Neither metric is automatically preferable.

### Fixed k does not mean fixed spatial radius

We now draw another 2,000 observations from the same domain, concentrating
the first coordinate toward the left with a scaled Beta(2,5) distribution.
The function and `k = 25` remain unchanged. This is a changed sampling design,
not a repeat measurement at the original locations.

```{r density-data, cache=TRUE, dependson="two-data"}
set.seed(22063)
X_dense <- cbind(6 * rbeta(2000, 2, 5) - 3, runif(2000, -3, 3))
density_control <- knn.basins(X_dense, f2(X_dense), k = 25,
                              min.persistence = .3, min.basin.size = 100)
```

```{r sampling-radius, echo=FALSE, fig.width=8.4, fig.height=4.4, fig.cap="Distance to the 25th other neighbor under L2, with a common color scale. The denser left region needs a smaller physical radius to collect 25 neighbors, while the sparse right region needs a larger radius. These are directed kNN radii; symmetrization can add longer incoming connections. Counts of assigned observations therefore measure sampling support, not geometric area.", fig.alt="Uniform and left-concentrated samples colored by a shared scale of 25th-neighbor radius."}
local({
    op <- par(no.readonly = TRUE); on.exit(par(op))
    layout(matrix(c(1, 2, 3, 3), 2, 2, byrow = TRUE), heights = c(1, .16))
    palette <- hcl.colors(128, "Viridis")
    limits <- range(c(two$neighborhood$radius, density_control$neighborhood$radius))
    for (i in 1:2) {
        xx <- if (i == 1) X2 else X_dense
        rr <- if (i == 1) two$neighborhood$radius else density_control$neighborhood$radius
        color <- palette[pmax(1, pmin(128, 1 + floor(127 * (rr - limits[1]) / diff(limits))))]
        theme_par(mar = c(3.1, 3.5, 2, 1), mgp = c(1.9, .6, 0), cex.axis = .85)
        plot(xx, asp = 1, pch = 16, cex = .45, col = color, xlim = c(-3, 3), ylim = c(-3, 3),
             xlab = "Coordinate 1", ylab = "Coordinate 2",
             main = if (i == 1) "Uniform sampling" else "Concentrated toward the left", cex.main = .95)
    }
    theme_par(mar = c(2.6, 5, .1, 4), mgp = c(1.5, .4, 0))
    image(seq(limits[1], limits[2], length.out = 128), c(0, 1), matrix(1:128, 128, 2),
          col = palette, yaxt = "n", xlab = "25th-neighbor radius (coordinate units)", ylab = "", cex.axis = .8)
})
```

## 3. Maunga Whau: extrema of a real terrain grid

R's [`datasets::volcano` documentation](https://stat.ethz.ch/R-manual/R-devel/library/datasets/html/volcano.html)
describes topography of Maunga Whau (Mt Eden), digitized from a map by Ross
Ihaka, on an 87-by-61 grid with 10-m spacing. It cautions that the data should
not be regarded as accurate. This is an illustrative terrain analysis, not
validation against a surveyed reference surface.

Each grid location becomes one row of `X`, giving 5,307 observations. The
two coordinates below are local offsets along the matrix axes in metres;
the figures do not assert a geographic origin or compass orientation.
Heights and persistence are reported in the dataset's height units. The
supplied heights are used directly, including exact ties, without smoothing.

```{r terrain-data, cache=TRUE}
terrain_grid <- datasets::volcano
grid_index <- expand.grid(row = seq_len(nrow(terrain_grid)),
                           column = seq_len(ncol(terrain_grid)))
Xv <- cbind(row.offset = 10 * (grid_index$row - 1),
             column.offset = 10 * (grid_index$column - 1))
yv <- as.vector(terrain_grid)
stopifnot(identical(yv, as.vector(terrain_grid[as.matrix(grid_index)])))
terrain <- knn.basins(Xv, yv, k = 50, metric = "L2",
                      min.persistence = 5, min.basin.size = 100,
                      symmetrize = TRUE)
```

```{r terrain-details, echo=FALSE}
terrain_boundary <- boundary_extrema(terrain, Xv, "min")
terrain_min_table <- terrain$min$extrema
terrain_min_table$boundary <- terrain_boundary
interior_v <- terrain_min_table[!terrain_boundary & terrain_min_table$retained, ]
stopifnot(nrow(interior_v) == 1L)
contours_v <- list(x = sort(unique(Xv[, 1])), y = sort(unique(Xv[, 2])), z = terrain_grid,
                   levels = seq(100, 190, 15))
```

```{r terrain-overview, echo=FALSE, fig.width=9, fig.height=2.7, fig.cap="Left: the supplied terrain heights with contours labeled in dataset height units; the interior retained minimum is marked, and the dashed contour shows its kNN merge level. Center and right: final maximum-oriented and minimum-oriented assignments, respectively. White triangles identify retained extrema. Colors identify different basin partitions in the two directions. Offsets follow matrix axes, not a claimed geographic orientation.", fig.alt="The volcano elevation grid beside its final maximum and minimum basin maps, with an interior depression marked."}
local({
    op <- par(no.readonly = TRUE); on.exit(par(op)); par(mfrow = c(1, 3))
    theme_par(mar = c(3.2, 3.2, 2.1, .7), mgp = c(1.9, .6, 0), cex.axis = .8, cex.lab = .86)
    image(contours_v$x, contours_v$y, terrain_grid, col = hcl.colors(64, "Terrain"),
          asp = 1, useRaster = TRUE, xlab = "Row-axis offset (m)", ylab = "Column-axis offset (m)",
          main = "Supplied terrain heights", cex.main = .93, xaxs = "i", yaxs = "i")
    contour(contours_v$x, contours_v$y, terrain_grid, add = TRUE, levels = contours_v$levels,
            col = "#263b4388", labcex = .65)
    contour(contours_v$x, contours_v$y, terrain_grid, add = TRUE,
            levels = interior_v$merge.level, drawlabels = FALSE, lty = 2, lwd = 1.3, col = ink)
    points(Xv[interior_v$row, 1], Xv[interior_v$row, 2], pch = 25, bg = "white", cex = 1.2)
    mtext(sprintf("Interior %.0f; merge %.0f", interior_v$value, interior_v$merge.level), side = 3, cex = .7, line = .1)
    basin_map(Xv, terrain, "max", "labels", "Final basins toward maxima", contours_v,
              raster_dim = dim(terrain_grid))
    basin_map(Xv, terrain, "min", "labels", "Final basins toward minima", contours_v,
              raster_dim = dim(terrain_grid))
})
```

```{r terrain-stages, echo=FALSE, fig.width=9, fig.height=2.7, fig.cap="Minimum-oriented terrain basins before merging, after persistence merging, and after size filtering. Colors remain tied to the original representative rows. Persistence merging reduces the number of basins; at this setting the minimum-size filter makes no further change. Boundary markers remain visible even when their numerical labels would fall outside the plot.", fig.alt="Three maps showing the volcano minimum basins through initial assignment, persistence merging and minimum-size filtering."}
local({
    op <- par(no.readonly = TRUE); on.exit(par(op)); par(mfrow = c(1, 3))
    for (i in 1:3) basin_map(Xv, terrain, "min",
        c("initial.labels", "persistence.labels", "labels")[i],
        c("Initial minima", "After persistence merging", "After size filtering")[i],
        contours_v, raster_dim = dim(terrain_grid))
})
```

The interior minimum has height `r interior_v$value` and joins an older
minimum at height `r interior_v$merge.level`, giving persistence
**`r interior_v$merge.level` - `r interior_v$value` = `r interior_v$persistence`**.
Its final basin contains `r interior_v$merged.size` observations. Raising
the minimum size from 100 to 150 would exclude this basin despite its
substantial vertical separation. This follows from the assigned count, not
from an assessment of whether the depression is scientifically important.

```{r terrain-table, echo=FALSE}
knitr::kable(terrain_min_table[, c("row", "value", "merge.level", "persistence",
                                   "plateau.size", "merged.size", "boundary", "status")],
              digits = 0, caption = "All original terrain minima. Boundary is true if any row of the extremum plateau touches the grid boundary.")
```

Of the `r sum(terrain_min_table$retained)` retained minima,
`r sum(terrain_min_table$retained & terrain_min_table$boundary)` touch the
sampled boundary. Their interpretation depends on the chosen extent. The
essential minimum has infinite persistence because no older minimum exists
in its connected component; infinity is not a measure of statistical certainty.

Regular grids have equal-distance neighbors, and the recorded heights have
exact plateaus. Symmetric mode breaks distance ties by row index and contracts
connected equal-height plateaus. We preserve the stated matrix order and do
not add jitter. Row permutations can change a tied kNN cutoff. L2/Linfty
comparisons therefore reflect both the metric and its associated tie pattern.

### Symmetric and asymmetric modes at fixed settings

We now compare the two modes on the **same 5,307 locations and supplied
heights**, using **L2, `k = 50`, `min.persistence = 5`, and
`min.basin.size = 100`** throughout. Only `symmetrize` changes in the call.
That switch selects a complete convention: union neighborhoods, connected
plateaus, and level-set persistence in symmetric mode; outgoing neighborhoods,
individual terminal rows, and directed escape prominence in asymmetric mode.
The common threshold is five dataset height units, but the two prominence
definitions need not give the same value. This comparison does not isolate
edge symmetrization from the change in plateau and prominence rules.

```{r terrain-mode-fit, cache=TRUE, dependson="terrain-data"}
terrain_asymmetric <- knn.basins(
    Xv, yv, k = 50, metric = "L2",
    min.persistence = 5, min.basin.size = 100,
    symmetrize = FALSE
)
```

```{r terrain-mode-summary, include=FALSE}
terrain_modes <- list(Symmetric = terrain, Asymmetric = terrain_asymmetric)
terrain_mode_table <- do.call(rbind, lapply(c("max", "min"), function(d) {
    do.call(rbind, lapply(names(terrain_modes), function(mode) {
        z <- terrain_modes[[mode]][[d]]
        data.frame(mode = mode, direction = d, initial = nrow(z$extrema),
                   essential = sum(z$extrema$essential),
                   after.merging = length(unique(z$persistence.labels)),
                   retained = length(z$basins), unassigned = sum(is.na(z$labels)),
                   unassigned.percent = 100 * mean(is.na(z$labels)))
    }))
}))
# A representative row has the same color in both modes within a direction.
# Different row identifiers remain distinct even when their heights are equal.
terrain_mode_colors <- lapply(c("max", "min"), function(d) {
    rows <- sort(unique(unlist(lapply(terrain_modes, function(fit)
        fit[[d]]$extrema$row[fit[[d]]$extrema$retained]))))
    stopifnot(length(rows) <= length(basin_palette))
    original_rows <- terrain[[d]]$extrema$row
    original_colors <- setNames(rep(basin_palette, length.out = length(original_rows)), original_rows)
    key <- original_colors[as.character(rows)]
    names(key) <- as.character(rows)
    missing <- is.na(key)
    key[missing] <- setdiff(basin_palette, key[!missing])[seq_len(sum(missing))]
    key
})
names(terrain_mode_colors) <- c("max", "min")
terrain_interior_table <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(terrain_modes), function(mode) {
    tab <- terrain_modes[[mode]]$min$extrema
    z <- tab[match(interior_v$row, tab$row), ]
    stopifnot(nrow(z) == 1L, !is.na(z$row), z$retained)
    data.frame(mode = mode, row = z$row, height = z$value,
               merge.or.escape.level = z$merge.level, prominence = z$persistence,
               assigned.rows = z$merged.size)
}))
asym_min <- terrain_asymmetric$min$extrema
asym_min_summary <- terrain_mode_table[terrain_mode_table$mode == "Asymmetric" &
                                      terrain_mode_table$direction == "min", ]
```

```{r terrain-mode-comparison, echo=FALSE, fig.width=9, fig.height=8.7, fig.cap="Final volcano basins with L2, k = 50, prominence threshold 5 height units, and minimum assigned size 100 in both modes. Columns compare symmetric and asymmetric neighborhoods; rows compare maxima and minima on identical coordinate scales. Within each direction, the same representative row has the same color across modes, without implying identical basin membership. Gray cells are unassigned after size filtering. White triangles mark retained extrema; nearby boundary markers can overlap. The legend identifies minimum-basin representative rows.", fig.alt="Four panels compare final symmetric and asymmetric volcano basins. Both maximum panels contain one basin. The minimum panels contain five versus nine basins; the asymmetric panel also has 199 gray unassigned observations."}
local({
    op <- par(no.readonly = TRUE); on.exit(par(op))
    layout(matrix(c(1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 5), nrow = 3, byrow = TRUE), heights = c(1, 1, .24))
    for (d in c("max", "min")) for (mode in names(terrain_modes)) {
        fit <- terrain_modes[[mode]]
        z <- fit[[d]]
        basin_map(Xv, fit, d, "labels",
                  paste(if (d == "max") "Maxima:" else "Minima:", tolower(mode)),
                  contours_v, raster_dim = dim(terrain_grid),
                  color_key = terrain_mode_colors[[d]], padding = .025,
                  subtitle = sprintf("%d retained; %d unassigned", length(z$basins), sum(is.na(z$labels))))
    }
    theme_par(mar = c(0, 0, 0, 0))
    plot.new()
    legend("center", legend = c(names(terrain_mode_colors$min), "Unassigned"),
           fill = c(unname(terrain_mode_colors$min), excluded), border = NA,
           ncol = 5, bty = "n", cex = .83, title = "Minimum-basin representative rows")
})
```

```{r terrain-mode-table, echo=FALSE}
knitr::kable(terrain_mode_table[, c("mode", "direction", "initial", "after.merging",
                                   "retained", "unassigned", "unassigned.percent")],
              col.names = c("Mode", "Direction", "Initial", "After merging", "Final",
                            "Unassigned", "Unassigned (%)"), digits = 2, row.names = FALSE,
              caption = "Fixed-setting comparison. Initial and merged assignments cover all 5,307 observations; only the size filter creates unassigned rows.")
```

Both modes finish with the same single maximum basin, containing all 5,307
observations. The minimum partition changes: symmetric mode retains
`r sum(terrain$min$extrema$retained)` basins and assigns every observation;
asymmetric mode retains `r asym_min_summary$retained` basins and leaves
`r asym_min_summary$unassigned` observations
(`r sprintf("%.2f", asym_min_summary$unassigned.percent)`%) unassigned.
In asymmetric mode, `r asym_min_summary$after.merging` minimum basins survive
the prominence threshold, and the separate size filter removes
`r asym_min_summary$after.merging - asym_min_summary$retained` of them.

Part of the larger initial count comes from the treatment of equal heights.
The lowest recorded height, `r min(yv)`, occurs at `r sum(yv == min(yv))`
locations. Symmetric mode combines these connected locations into one
essential minimum plateau. Asymmetric mode keeps all
`r sum(asym_min$essential)` as separate essential terminal minima because
no strictly lower outcome exists. Most of those terminal rows support fewer
than 100 assigned observations after merging and fail the size filter.
These counts describe the two definitions; they do not rank their scientific
validity or establish additional physical depressions.

The interior depression provides a useful comparison of membership rather
than counts alone. Its representative row, height, and merge/escape level
agree across modes, giving prominence 16 in both. Its assigned support
increases from `r terrain_interior_table$assigned.rows[1]` to
`r terrain_interior_table$assigned.rows[2]` observations. Equal prominence
therefore does not imply an identical basin boundary.

```{r terrain-interior-comparison, echo=FALSE}
knitr::kable(terrain_interior_table, row.names = FALSE,
              col.names = c("Mode", "Row", "Height", "Merge/escape level", "Prominence", "Assigned rows"),
              caption = "The same interior minimum under both neighborhood conventions; heights and prominence use dataset height units.")
```

## Sensitivity to neighborhood scale and distance

This section uses symmetric mode throughout. We keep outcomes and filtering
thresholds fixed within each example and compare `k = 25, 50, 100`. The
two-dimensional and terrain examples use both
metrics. In one dimension the metrics are mathematically identical; the
numerical check below compares them at `k = 25`.

| Example | Observations | Persistence threshold | Minimum assigned size |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Exact 1D | 1,000 | 0.25 outcome units | 100 (10%) |
| Exact 2D | 2,000 | 0.30 outcome units | 100 (5%) |
| Terrain | 5,307 | 5 dataset height units | 100 (1.88%) |

```{r sensitivity-fits, cache=TRUE, dependson=c("one-data", "two-data", "terrain-data")}
sensitivity_inputs <- list(
    `Exact 1D` = list(X = X1, y = y1, p = .25, metrics = "L2"),
    `Exact 2D` = list(X = X2, y = y2, p = .3, metrics = c("L2", "Linfty")),
    Terrain = list(X = Xv, y = yv, p = 5, metrics = c("L2", "Linfty"))
)
sensitivity_fits <- list()
for (name in names(sensitivity_inputs)) {
    input <- sensitivity_inputs[[name]]
    for (metric in input$metrics) for (k in c(25L, 50L, 100L)) {
        key <- paste(name, metric, k, sep = ":")
        sensitivity_fits[[key]] <- if (name == "Exact 1D" && k == 25) one else
            if (name == "Exact 2D" && metric == "L2" && k == 25) two else
            if (name == "Exact 2D" && metric == "Linfty" && k == 25) two_linf else
            if (name == "Terrain" && metric == "L2" && k == 50) terrain else
            knn.basins(input$X, input$y, k, metric,
                       min.persistence = input$p, min.basin.size = 100)
    }
}
```

```{r sensitivity-summary, include=FALSE}
sensitivity_table <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(sensitivity_fits), function(key) {
    fit <- sensitivity_fits[[key]]
    example <- strsplit(key, ":", fixed = TRUE)[[1]][1]
    do.call(rbind, lapply(c("max", "min"), function(d) {
        z <- fit[[d]]
        data.frame(example = example, metric = fit$parameters$metric, k = fit$parameters$k,
                   direction = d, initial = nrow(z$extrema), retained = sum(z$extrema$retained),
                   unassigned.percent = 100 * mean(is.na(z$labels)),
                   components = fit$neighborhood$n.components)
    }))
}))
stage_table <- do.call(rbind, list(summary_stages(one, "Exact 1D"), summary_stages(noisy, "Noisy 1D"),
                                 summary_stages(two, "Exact 2D"), summary_stages(terrain, "Terrain")))
```

```{r sensitivity-figure, echo=FALSE, fig.width=9, fig.height=6.1, fig.cap="Retained extrema counts (top) and percentages of unassigned observations (bottom) as k changes. Blue denotes maxima and gold denotes minima; solid circles denote L2 and dashed triangles denote Linfty. Outcomes and thresholds are fixed within each example. Coincident curves overlap; the table below reports every series. The one-dimensional panel shows L2 because the two metrics coincide there. Count agreement does not establish identical locations or memberships.", fig.alt="Six sensitivity panels reporting retained maximum and minimum counts and percentages excluded at k 25, 50 and 100."}
local({
    op <- par(no.readonly = TRUE); on.exit(par(op)); par(mfrow = c(2, 3), oma = c(1.2, 0, 1.9, 0))
    for (measure in c("retained", "unassigned.percent")) for (name in names(sensitivity_inputs)) {
        tab <- sensitivity_table[sensitivity_table$example == name, ]
        theme_par(mar = c(3, 3.5, 1.8, .8), mgp = c(2.2, .6, 0), cex.axis = .83)
        ymax <- if (measure == "retained") max(sensitivity_table$retained) else max(sensitivity_table$unassigned.percent)
        plot(c(25, 100), c(0, max(1, ymax) * 1.1), type = "n", xaxt = "n",
             xlab = "k (other neighbors)", ylab = if (measure == "retained") "Retained extrema" else "Unassigned (%)",
             main = name, cex.main = .95)
        axis(1, at = c(25, 50, 100))
        for (d in c("max", "min")) for (metric in unique(tab$metric)) {
            zz <- tab[tab$direction == d & tab$metric == metric, ]
            color <- if (d == "max") "#216b9b" else "#b78016"
            lines(zz$k, zz[[measure]], type = "b", col = color, lwd = 1.5,
                   lty = if (metric == "L2") 1 else 2, pch = if (metric == "L2") 16 else 2, cex = .85)
        }
    }
    mtext("Blue: maxima   Gold: minima        Circle / solid: L2   Triangle / dashed: Linfty",
           side = 3, outer = TRUE, line = .2, cex = .8, col = ink)
})
```

```{r sensitivity-table, echo=FALSE}
knitr::kable(sensitivity_table, digits = 2, row.names = FALSE,
              caption = "Numerical values behind the sensitivity figure; connected-component counts are included.")
```

The thresholds above are teaching choices, not universal recommendations.
Changes in `k` alter connectivity as well as the local extremum test. Compare
locations and basin overlap when tracking features across settings; raw row
labels can change. A small unassigned fraction can still include an important
narrow feature. Conversely, a stable feature count can conceal changing
memberships.

## Numerical checks and interpretation limits

The checks accompanying this vignette use the displayed inputs and stored
results. They verify:

* conservation of all observations before size filtering and exact accounting
  of retained and unassigned observations afterward;
* persistence merging by following the reported parent relationships, with
  threshold equality retained and essential extrema preserved;
* finite merge levels using an independent threshold-connectivity search on
  the returned neighborhoods, for every original extremum in the four main fits;
* nearest neighbors against direct distance calculations at selected rows;
* maximum/minimum sign reversal, one-dimensional metric equality, and the
  alignment between terrain cells, coordinates, and outcome values;
* recovery of the 1D function's stationary extrema using roots of its analytic
  derivative, separately from the discrete graph construction;
* identical inputs and numeric settings for the two terrain modes, exact
  outgoing-neighbor extrema and shortest improving steps for every asymmetric
  terrain row, and directed escape levels and parent targets using an
  independent threshold-reachability search for all asymmetric terrain extrema.

```{r numerical-verification, include=FALSE}
verification <- data.frame(check = character(), cases = integer(), passed = logical())
record_check <- function(name, cases, condition) {
    stopifnot(isTRUE(condition))
    verification <<- rbind(verification, data.frame(check = name, cases = cases, passed = TRUE))
}
all_fits <- c(list(one = one, noisy = noisy, two = two, terrain = terrain,
                  terrain_asymmetric = terrain_asymmetric, density = density_control), sensitivity_fits)
for (fit in all_fits) for (d in c("max", "min")) {
    result <- fit[[d]]; tab <- result$extrema; n <- length(fit$y)
    stopifnot(sum(tab$initial.size) == n, sum(tab$merged.size) == n,
              !anyNA(result$initial.labels), !anyNA(result$persistence.labels))
    for (i in seq_len(nrow(tab))) {
        stopifnot(tab$initial.size[i] == sum(result$initial.labels == tab$row[i]),
                  tab$merged.size[i] == sum(result$persistence.labels == tab$row[i]))
        root <- i
        while (!tab$essential[root] && tab$persistence[root] < fit$parameters$min.persistence) {
            root <- match(tab$parent.row[root], tab$row)
            stopifnot(!is.na(root))
        }
        stopifnot(tab$persistence.root[i] == tab$row[root])
    }
    expected <- tab$persistence.root[match(result$initial.labels, tab$row)]
    stopifnot(identical(result$persistence.labels, expected))
    size <- tab$merged.size[match(expected, tab$row)]
    expected[size < fit$parameters$min.basin.size] <- NA_integer_
    stopifnot(identical(result$labels, expected),
              identical(sort(unlist(result$basins, use.names = FALSE)), which(!is.na(result$labels))),
              all(tab$merged.size[tab$retained] >= fit$parameters$min.basin.size))
}
record_check("Assignment and filtering accounting", 2L * length(all_fits), TRUE)

# Independent oracle: binary search the observed thresholds, using BFS to
# determine when this peak reaches any elder. No merge-tree code is called.
oracle_merge <- function(graph, field, peak) {
    n <- length(field)
    elder <- field > field[peak] | (field == field[peak] & seq_len(n) < peak)
    same_component <- graph$component == graph$component[peak]
    if (!any(elder & same_component)) return(NA_real_)
    reaches_elder <- function(level) {
        allowed <- field >= level
        seen <- rep(FALSE, n); seen[peak] <- TRUE
        queue <- integer(n); queue[1] <- peak; head <- 1L; tail <- 1L
        while (head <= tail) {
            v <- queue[head]; head <- head + 1L
            if (elder[v]) return(TRUE)
            neighbors <- graph$adj.list[[v]]
            add <- neighbors[allowed[neighbors] & !seen[neighbors]]
            if (length(add)) {
                seen[add] <- TRUE
                queue[tail + seq_along(add)] <- add
                tail <- tail + length(add)
            }
        }
        FALSE
    }
    levels <- sort(unique(field[field <= field[peak] & same_component]), decreasing = TRUE)
    lo <- 1L; hi <- length(levels)
    while (lo < hi) {
        mid <- (lo + hi) %/% 2L
        if (reaches_elder(levels[mid])) hi <- mid else lo <- mid + 1L
    }
    levels[lo]
}
oracle_count <- 0L
for (fit in list(one, noisy, two, terrain)) for (d in c("max", "min")) {
    tab <- fit[[d]]$extrema; field <- if (d == "max") fit$y else -fit$y
    for (i in seq_len(nrow(tab))) {
        level <- oracle_merge(fit$neighborhood, field, tab$row[i])
        expected <- if (d == "max") tab$merge.level[i] else -tab$merge.level[i]
        stopifnot(isTRUE(all.equal(level, expected, tolerance = 1e-12)))
        oracle_count <- oracle_count + 1L
    }
}
record_check("Independent threshold-connectivity merge levels", oracle_count, TRUE)

distance_count <- 0L
for (case in list(list(X1, one), list(X2, two), list(X2, two_linf), list(Xv, terrain))) {
    X <- case[[1]]; fit <- case[[2]]
    for (i in unique(as.integer(seq(1, nrow(X), length.out = 12)))) {
        delta <- abs(sweep(X, 2, X[i, ], "-"))
        distance <- if (fit$parameters$metric == "L2") sqrt(rowSums(delta^2)) else apply(delta, 1, max)
        distance[i] <- Inf
        expected <- order(distance, seq_len(nrow(X)))[seq_len(fit$parameters$k)]
        # For random non-tied distances, direct and scaled L2 arithmetic agree
        # in rank. Integer terrain differences give exact cutoff tie groups.
        stopifnot(identical(fit$neighborhood$knn.index[i, ], expected),
                  isTRUE(all.equal(fit$neighborhood$knn.distance[i, ], distance[expected], tolerance = 1e-12)))
        distance_count <- distance_count + 1L
    }
}
record_check("Direct-distance neighbor rows", distance_count, TRUE)
one_linf <- knn.basins(X1, y1, 25, "Linfty", min.persistence = .25, min.basin.size = 100)
record_check("L2 equals Linfty in one dimension", 1L,
              identical(one$max, one_linf$max) && identical(one$min, one_linf$min))
opposite <- knn.basins(X2, -y2, 25, direction = "max", min.persistence = .3, min.basin.size = 100)
record_check("Minima equal maxima of the negated 2D field", 1L,
              identical(two$min$labels, opposite$max$labels) &&
              isTRUE(all.equal(two$min$extrema$persistence, opposite$max$extrema$persistence)))
f1_derivative <- function(x) rowSums(matrix(vapply(seq_len(nrow(components)), function(j) {
    with(components[j, ], -amplitude * (x - center) / width^2 * exp(-.5 * ((x - center) / width)^2))
}, numeric(length(x))), nrow = length(x)))
reference_grid <- seq(0, 10, length.out = 20001)
sgn <- sign(f1_derivative(reference_grid))
crossings <- which(diff(sgn) != 0)
stationary <- vapply(crossings, function(i)
    uniroot(f1_derivative, reference_grid[c(i, i + 1)], tol = 1e-12)$root, numeric(1))
is_maximum <- f1_derivative(stationary - 1e-5) > 0
for (d in c("max", "min")) {
    truth <- if (d == "max") stationary[is_maximum] else c(0, stationary[!is_maximum], 10)
    actual <- sort(X1[one[[d]]$extrema$row, 1])
    stopifnot(length(actual) == length(truth), max(abs(actual - sort(truth))) <= diff(X1[1:2, 1]))
}
record_check("1D continuous extrema locations within one sample interval", length(stationary) + 2L, TRUE)
record_check("Terrain coordinate/outcome alignment", length(yv),
              identical(yv, as.vector(terrain_grid[as.matrix(grid_index)])))
record_check("Known narrow synthetic peaks survive persistence but fail size", 2L,
              nrow(narrow1) == 1L && narrow1$persistence > .25 && narrow1$merged.size < 100 &&
              narrow2$status == "filtered_size" && narrow2$persistence > .3)
record_check("Interior terrain depression has height 148 and merge level 164", 1L,
              interior_v$value == 148 && interior_v$merge.level == 164 && interior_v$persistence == 16)

fixed_parameters <- c("k", "metric", "direction", "min.persistence", "min.basin.size",
                       "scaling", "projection", "smoothing", "distance.ties")
record_check("Terrain modes share input values, settings, and selected kNN", length(yv),
              identical(terrain$y, terrain_asymmetric$y) &&
              identical(terrain$parameters[fixed_parameters], terrain_asymmetric$parameters[fixed_parameters]) &&
              identical(terrain$neighborhood$knn.index, terrain_asymmetric$neighborhood$knn.index) &&
              identical(terrain$neighborhood$knn.distance, terrain_asymmetric$neighborhood$knn.distance))
for (d in c("max", "min")) {
    field <- if (d == "max") yv else -yv
    z <- terrain_asymmetric[[d]]
    terminal <- rep(FALSE, length(yv))
    for (i in seq_along(yv)) {
        neighbors <- terrain_asymmetric$neighborhood$adj.list[[i]]
        distance <- terrain_asymmetric$neighborhood$edge.length.list[[i]]
        stopifnot(identical(neighbors, sort(terrain$neighborhood$knn.index[i, ])))
        improve <- which(field[neighbors] > field[i])
        terminal[i] <- length(improve) == 0L
        expected <- if (terminal[i]) NA_integer_ else
            neighbors[improve[order(distance[improve], neighbors[improve])[1]]]
        stopifnot(identical(z$next.vertex[i], expected))
        endpoint <- i
        while (!is.na(z$next.vertex[endpoint])) endpoint <- z$next.vertex[endpoint]
        stopifnot(z$initial.labels[i] == endpoint)
    }
    stopifnot(setequal(z$extrema$row, which(terminal)))
}
record_check("Directed terrain per-row extrema and shortest improving paths", 2L * length(yv), TRUE)

# Independent directed oracle: search observed thresholds using outgoing BFS.
# Strictly better terminal rows are targets; equal-height terminals are not.
# No widest-path backend is used, and targets are resolved at the escape level.
oracle_directed_escape <- function(graph, field, peaks, peak) {
    target <- rep(FALSE, length(field))
    target[peaks[field[peaks] > field[peak]]] <- TRUE
    absent <- list(level = NA_real_, parent = NA_integer_)
    if (!any(target)) return(absent)
    reachable_targets <- function(level) {
        seen <- rep(FALSE, length(field)); seen[peak] <- TRUE
        queue <- integer(length(field)); queue[1] <- peak; head <- 1L; tail <- 1L
        while (head <= tail) {
            neighbors <- graph$adj.list[[queue[head]]]; head <- head + 1L
            add <- neighbors[field[neighbors] >= level & !seen[neighbors]]
            if (length(add)) {
                seen[add] <- TRUE
                queue[tail + seq_along(add)] <- add
                tail <- tail + length(add)
            }
        }
        which(seen & target)
    }
    levels <- sort(unique(field[field <= field[peak]]), decreasing = TRUE)
    if (!length(reachable_targets(tail(levels, 1)))) return(absent)
    lo <- 1L; hi <- length(levels)
    while (lo < hi) {
        mid <- (lo + hi) %/% 2L
        if (length(reachable_targets(levels[mid]))) hi <- mid else lo <- mid + 1L
    }
    targets <- reachable_targets(levels[lo])
    list(level = levels[lo], parent = targets[order(-field[targets], targets)][1])
}
directed_oracle_count <- 0L
for (d in c("max", "min")) {
    field <- if (d == "max") yv else -yv
    tab <- terrain_asymmetric[[d]]$extrema
    for (i in seq_len(nrow(tab))) {
        oracle <- oracle_directed_escape(terrain_asymmetric$neighborhood, field, tab$row, tab$row[i])
        level <- if (d == "max") tab$merge.level[i] else -tab$merge.level[i]
        persistence <- if (is.na(oracle$level)) Inf else field[tab$row[i]] - oracle$level
        stopifnot(isTRUE(all.equal(level, oracle$level)),
                  identical(tab$parent.row[i], oracle$parent),
                  isTRUE(all.equal(tab$persistence[i], persistence)))
        directed_oracle_count <- directed_oracle_count + 1L
    }
}
record_check("Independent directed terrain escape levels and parents", directed_oracle_count, TRUE)

expected_mode_counts <- rbind(c(3, 1, 1, 0), c(145, 1, 1, 0),

              setequal(lowest_plateau, which(yv == min(yv))) &&

knitr::kable(verification, row.names = FALSE,
              caption = "Executed checks. Cases have different meanings across rows and are not combined into an accuracy percentage.")
```

These checks establish consistency of the implementation and the reported
examples. They do not establish statistical significance, optimal thresholds,
or robustness on high-dimensional noisy data. Persistence measures separation
in the supplied outcome. Basin size measures assigned sample support.
Boundary effects, sampling density, metric choice, and any upstream smoothing
remain part of the scientific interpretation.

The complete source is installed with the vignette. For method details, see
`help("knn.basins", package = "gflow")`; for graph-input methods, see the
[canonical basin workflow](basin_complex_workflow_vignette.html).

the displayed outcomes. Cached chunks include the package code/build identity
and runtime identity, so changed implementations do not silently reuse results.
